text: Like a lot of our designs, we really start with a strong form, strong architecture, strong lines,
strong detailing, and we then pare it back, refine it, soften it, layers of materiality in the space
to create form and style of architecture which is strong, but then really softened and calming
and intense execution, and really ensuring that the space doesn't feel sterile or plain,
but something which is just perfectly aligned, considered, sculptural, but incredibly practical.
I'm Adam from Adam Kane Architects, architect and interior designer for this project.
So, the property is located about 15-20 minutes northeast of the Melbourne CBD.
We really wanted to have a home that was quite the statement architecturally,
but really softened through different layers of texture, and having the home really nestled
within a landscape, and having that really strong connection to the surrounding gardens.
The clients were quite flexible and accommodating with their brief.
They've got three young children, and really wanting a home that would be their forever home,
but the site did have its restraints being quite sloping, and the house being two stories at the
front, three at the rear. So, finding that balance of how that would work from a form,
from a layout, from a functionality. Also, what was really important is because they're
a quite a close family, wanting to make sure that there was still that connection with everyone,
and having perhaps a little bit of separation at times, but without being isolated.
So, from the street, the home has quite a strong series of monolithic forms and
private from its adjoining neighbours. And as you walk towards the home,
it starts revealing itself and has a much more open feel and sense.
As you walk through the front door, you get this little sightline throughout the building
out across the expansive horizon just this little glimpse of that vegetation and mountain range.
And then you walk into the the large double height foyer, you get this beautiful spiral stairs going
up and down across the three floors. And then the living, dining, kitchen opens itself up,
you get these expansive views, amazing light qualities. The space is beautifully balanced
with the feature brick running seamlessly from outside to in. You've got the amazing warmth
from the the veneer cabinetry concealing all of the mess and day-to-day essentials.
And then this amazing feature island bench of quite monolithic and sculptural. And then upstairs
on the for the home is all of the living, the the kids' bedrooms, the primary suite.
Having those moments where everyone can be together, but also have their own space.
We always design in a way that as one circulates, they were looking towards a different sightline,
a different garden, a subtle realisation there's a pool hidden behind a wall that
you can only get through as you're as you're walking around, a little glimpse of a staircase
from the kitchen area. The experiential qualities of this home is something that
makes it enjoyable to walk through and live through rather than being open all at once.
I recall early days asking the clients about how they cook and how they want to cook.
And often it can be divided into two categories, I suppose. Someone wants to be in the heart of
the action and kind of on display, and someone doesn't want to be bothered,
and that was the latter of those two was these particular clients. And for a house of this
calibre and the perfection that we all sought, we were wanting to use the Gaggenau products
and using them in a considered way to not be too overt with their placement.
I think what was particularly impressive with the expressive series of ovens by
Gaggenau is the attention to detail and the craftsmanship. The beautiful ventilation grill,
which we've recessed flush with the adjoining wall, the almost picture frame around the food,
this beautiful hand-finished stainless steel by a craftsman. They have a such a beautiful
execution to their design, and it was a real easy choice for us to go in that direction.
I think for us a common desire or request from a client is a timeless aesthetic, and
that's often why they'll come to us in the first place, and they seek this because it
is often their forever home and something that they want to feel really connected to.
So, the enduring quality of our designs in this home is that that monumentality that stands,
that grounding with the environment, that sense of permanence with the the forms,
the deep reveals, the design which feels like a quality and enduring home. So, I think decades
from now as someone walks past and see the gardens established and this home just nestled
in amongst it, it'll be very clear that you know, someone put a lot of time and thought into
ensuring these details are perfect and refined and in place with the home and the setting.
